clue.text: Sort of tie makes do without edge

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to do someone is to con or cheat them
a lip is the edge of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: A tie that does without a proper edge, a cheap shortcut to dressing smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, which is what makes the clue tricky; 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip-on is a ready-made tie that fastens to the collar with a clip rather than being knotted.

parts.note: a chain of bosses above workers, imagined as the running of railway tracks by the British rail infrastructure company

explanation.surface: A question about how the company that runs Britain's railway tracks organises its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Network Rail owns Britain's railway tracks; the joke is that a railway 'line' would naturally be managed by such a system.
explanation.definitionFit: Line management is the business arrangement where each employee reports to a direct superior in a chain.

clue.text: Having lots of mates in work, steady love with randy characters

indicators.note: the word love is placed in the middle of the word for working steadily

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at something, as in plying a trade
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of the following word are jumbled, as randy suggests

explanation.surface: Someone working steadily at love alongside some lusty types sounds like they have plenty of partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lots of mates in work' tempts as the definition; the definition stops at 'mates'. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyandry is the custom of a woman having more than one husband at the same time.

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Picking out which sightseeing trips in the Italian city are least unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicest is the superlative of nice, so the most pleasant and so the least unpleasant.

clue.text: Address for letter in which doctor's admitted endlessly relapsing state

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the doctor's abbreviation takes the other part inside it

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor; with the possessive it gives DRS

indicators.note: relapsing suggests falling back, so the shortened word is written backwards
endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Israel is a state in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A hospital letter about a patient admitted whose condition keeps relapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'relapsing state' tempts you to read a medical condition; the state is a country, cut short by 'endlessly' and turned back by 'relapsing' to give EARSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear Sirs is the traditional formal salutation that opens a business letter.

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublemaker shows strangely macho tendencies.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis the Menace is the naughty boy of the British children's comic The Beano. 'unusual' turns HE-MAN TENDENCIES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic character is a mischievous boy whose name has become shorthand for any young troublemaker.

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The old saying about preaching to the converted, followed by a football official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'senior linesman' looks like a football official; the 'lines' are lines of verse. 'converted' rearranges PREACH TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-poet is a chief or leading poet, and a poet is a writer of lines.

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a squawk is a loud harsh complaint

explanation.surface: A wife's noisy grumbling is stopped before it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaw is an old, now offensive, word for a Native American wife or woman.

clue.text: Created a stir getting lost on overlooking confined region

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: on means about or concerning, which is RE

indicators.note: getting lost means losing its shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone causes a commotion after getting lost on a site overlooking a confined region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting lost' rearranges the letters into STRICTEDAREA; in a down answer, 'overlooking' puts the piece for 'on' on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A restricted area is a zone where entry is limited to authorised people, so it is confined.

indicators.note: to boil is to churn and bubble, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchgoer having a boil lanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boil' looks like the thing being lanced, but it is the signal to rearrange LANCING A.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican belongs to the Church of England or another church in its communion.

definitions.meaning: a holiday spent on a ship touring ports

explanation.surface: A film star is spending his holiday on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise is a famous actor, and a cruise is a pleasure voyage taken as a holiday.

clue.text: Character in film having cast in post-war use?

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Asking which film character had a plaster cast after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' could be a film cast or a plaster cast; it rearranges IN POST-WAR USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Powers is the spoof secret agent played by Mike Myers in a series of comedy films.

parts.note: settled reads as ... off, and lying in a bed of one's own making is the saying about bearing the results of one's own actions

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a bed they made for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'you've made your bed, now lie in it' means facing the consequences of your choices; 'settled' hints at paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay the price is to suffer the consequences of one's own actions, as the bed saying describes.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the rest
cast means thrown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a go is a turn or attempt, like a pass in a game
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: An opera cast riots over a backstage pass or permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the opera's performers but rearranges RIOT to RITO, which goes about GO and LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Every object stitched up on underside of chap's cloak

indicators.note: in a down answer, the chap sits above, with the other part on its underside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: up in a down answer means written from bottom to top, so the words are reversed

parts.note: every means all
it can stand for any object

explanation.surface: Every item is sewn into the lining of a man's cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitched up' turns ALL IT into TILLA, placed below MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk scarf or light cloak worn over the head and shoulders, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Proclaimed ruler of legendary characters around years before German assent

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the other pieces
the characters, or letters, of the word are rearranged
before means the years come ahead of the German word

parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A ruler proclaimed in the days of legend, years before a German said yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges the letters of 'legendary' into LADNEGREY. She was proclaimed queen of England in 1553 and reigned only nine days, never crowned.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Jane Grey was proclaimed Queen of England in 1553 but deposed after nine days, never crowned.

indicators.note: inhaled means drawn in, so one letter goes inside the cigar

parts.note: a stogy is a long, cheap cigar

explanation.surface: A heavy cigar whose smoke a daughter breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is heavy and filling, and a stodgy style is dull and weighty.

parts.note: to go is to depart
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone goes mad and is detained under mental health law.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, being 'sectioned' means being detained under the Mental Health Act; here it means divided into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Departmental means organised into departments, so divided into sections.

indicators.note: the possessive 's reads as has, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: Princess Diana, born Diana Spencer, is shaking with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze, so as an adjective it means trembling.

clue.text: Our Junior Correspondent's written about punishment involving president

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the punishment word wraps around the letter

parts.note: penal relates to punishment, as in penal servitude

explanation.surface: A newspaper's young reporter writes about a president's punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our Junior Correspondent' looks like a newspaper's reporter; it means a young person someone exchanges letters with. 's written about' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is a friend, often a child, with whom one keeps up a correspondence by letter.

clue.text: Sounding right, German car forges ahead

indicators.note: the car forges ahead, so it goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker
a Tory is a conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A German car speeds ahead, sounding just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory means relating to hearing, so concerned with sounding.

clue.text: Individual resting in coach for a time

indicators.note: one piece rests in the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A lone traveller is sitting in a coach for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is a prehistoric period when tools were made of stone.

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Oman is a state in Arabia

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned civil servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was historically a servant or attendant in a noble household, as in Yeoman of the Guard.
